newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.65 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.65 pct in May.

text.p: Brazil's real closed at 1.0704 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market, up 0.35 percent on the day but down 0.65 percent for the month, dealers said.
Earlier today the Central Bank depreciated the mini-band by 0.09 percent to between 1.0700 and 1.0750 reais per dollar. The mini-band fell 0.61 percent during May, the same as in April.

The real's rise Friday in the spot commercial market was due to dollar inflows and arbitrage with the future dollar market, dealers said. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $45 million surplus.

The real was also supported by banks that had been holding dollars over the last few days and sold them today in order to arbitrage with the dollar futures market. Futures closing price today will be used on June contracts, which will be settled on Monday.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0756 per greenback, down 0.09 percent on the day and 0.66 percent on the month.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.18 percent on the day and 0.62 percent in May, closing at 1.130 per dollar.
